en.title: Nicolas Cage Roasts MCU as a 'Glorified WWE' and Misses Storytelling
en.summary: The legendary actor Nicolas Cage has voiced his strong opinions on the current state of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, comparing it to a "well-funded and glorified WWE." He laments a perceived shift away from compelling narratives towards spectacle.
en.body:
Nicolas Cage, an actor whose career is as vibrant and unpredictable as the characters he embodies, has offered a candid assessment of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. In a recent public appearance, the Oscar winner didn't hold back, likening the sprawling superhero franchise to "a well-funded and glorified WWE." For Cage, the issue isn't necessarily the talent involved, but the direction the storytelling has taken.

He expressed a clear longing for the days when MCU films prioritized intricate narratives and character development. "It started out, in my view, terrific. Some of the early stories were marvelous," Cage remarked, recalling how the initial entries masterfully wove together diverse character arcs and backstories. However, he feels that recent installments have increasingly leaned into action sequences at the expense of meaningful plot, a shift he finds disappointing.

## A Shift in Focus

Cage's colorful analogy paints a vivid picture of his perception. He humorously noted that witnessing "50-plus, otherwise intelligent, remarkably gifted thespians putting on these ridiculous outfits and getting ready for the fight" reminds him distinctly of professional wrestling. This observation highlights his belief that the spectacle has overshadowed the substance, turning cinematic universes into elaborate, albeit expensive, action showcases rather than compelling dramatic pieces. He specifically mentioned wanting to see the MCU "get back to telling the stories and not just cutting to the wrestling match."

## What the Fans Are Saying

This critique from a respected actor like Nicolas Cage is likely to resonate with a significant portion of the filmgoing community. Many fans have openly discussed their own feelings about the MCU's evolution, with some echoing Cage's sentiment that the focus has shifted too heavily towards interconnected plotting and large-scale battles, sometimes at the cost of individual film's narrative integrity. The debate over whether superhero films should lean more into character-driven drama or high-octane action is a recurring theme among cinephiles and casual viewers alike. Cage's comments provide a high-profile voice to this ongoing discussion, framing it as a potential loss of narrative depth for a franchise that once captivated audiences with its ambitious storytelling.

## What's Next

While Nicolas Cage's latest cinematic endeavors continue to explore unique and compelling characters, the Marvel Cinematic Universe marches on with its ambitious slate of films and Disney+ series. Fans eager to see the direction of the MCU will be looking forward to upcoming projects, with the hope that they might recapture some of the narrative magic Cage seems to miss.
